title: In Good Time — What's new in Omagma v0.2.19
author: Actual Claude Opus 5.5 at xhigh (creative direction, copy, timing, camera, design)
baseline: Last user-approved film: v0.2.18 Heavy Lifting clarity cut (SHA256 aa431ff461eac89d368f7e97d8f5cbe7b18027d70113653544df02211c812ddf, 84.233333 s, 2527 frames, approved 2026-11-03). This film covers only changes since then.

music.source: Approved v0.2.7 final soundtrack via video/cache/short0218/audio/approved-flow-84.m4a (SHA256 4f849b3de93b24d841a81baa3a96177ef40deaeefeaefa07db768438c3fa854e), packet-copied unchanged

clockDecision: Five announced stories at 81 frames of announce+read each plus a 10-frame fold leave 1,610 demo frames (avg 10.7 s) inside the approved 84.233 s soundtrack, so nothing is rushed. The calendar hero gets the longest demo (12.6 s). The restored draft lands on the closing-phrase attack (2114); the recap spans the last phrase (2369) and the outro flare lands on the stop (2442).
narrationPolicy: Each feature beat owns exactly one kicker, one headline and one supporting line (the draft beat adds one footnote).
announceStart → textSettled (24 frames: kicker, headline words, typed supporting line) plays over the empty atmosphere; no UI is visible.
textSettled → demoStart is a 57-frame (1.9 s) reading gap with no UI and no text motion.
demoStart → demoEnd: the genuine UI opens from its seam and acts; narration stays fixed and fully settled. Only action keycaps appear, each 20 frames before its real press.
demoEnd → out: the UI folds back into its seam (10 frames) while the narration fades, leaving an empty stage for the next announcement.
Every demonstration ends on a populated result: Day grid in the new look, guest added, accepted invitation in the grid, the bill reminder in the due date's Day view, the restored words.
No separate payoff card: the restored draft folds directly into the recap (2200).
decisions: Order: Calendar grid & look (hero) → guest suggestions → RSVP → personal .ics reminder → discard & undo → recap → outro. Calendar stories sit together; the undo payoff takes the closing-phrase attack.

Calendar hero: genuine 104-column Week at full width (26.5 px), a contextual push into today's column of blocks with the genuine red now line in the blank row between earlier and later events (supporting context, not a repeated feature), then Day (2), where the overlapping pair genuinely splits into side-by-side lanes, then Ctrl+T Classic and Ctrl+T back, ending on the populated Orange & Blue Day.

Product constraint (current source, min_lane_cells = 8): a 104-column Week column is too narrow for two lanes, so its overlap is drawn as the genuine '+1' overflow; side-by-side overlap is shown only in Day. No wider, sub-26 px Week and no altered pixels.

Guests: the popup appears after two letters with nothing selected; the viewer reads 'Alex Example <alex@example.test>' before a deliberate ↓ and Enter add it. Copy says only your pick is added; no invitation is implied.
RSVP: one clean Accept. Copy claims nothing happens until y; the result shows the event still in the grid with its answer and the genuine status.

ICS: an everyday personal case ('Bill due?') from fictional Harbor Utilities, explicitly not a meeting invitation and not the v0.2.18 haircut. No 'no email' marketing claim. The populated due-date Day view is the result, reached by a hard cut.
Draft: typed words → Ctrl+X review → Ctrl+X discarded (populated mail with the genuine undo status) → Ctrl+Z restores the identical words. Footnote scopes :restore-draft to 7 days; no Gmail claim.
Ember: vertical travel only in the margin 30 px left of the frame, resting beside the spotlit row; it never crosses glyphs. No recorded pointer is used in this film.

Native states switch atomically on the press frame; camera glides only between identical-grid captures of one session (READY rejects mixed grids in a shot). Camera and spotlight rectangles stay separate.
Legibility: crops are bound by a 34 px ceiling as well as 1 image px per CSS px, so small dialogs never balloon; qa warns below 26 px.
Calendar frames carry a faint cool rim in their molten halo, a nod to the Orange & Blue look; everything else keeps the approved v0.2.18 magma design.
Poster is the film's own frame at 13.4 s: the Orange & Blue Day with its side-by-side lanes spotlit under the headline.

Composed-still review fixes (no timing, copy or music change): spotlight padding is 10 px horizontal / 3 px vertical so the wash edge stays in the inter-row gap and never slices glyphs; dialog/modal cameras are exact border boxes, so no partial background words show; all draft cameras use the full 96-column width below the header row; Day cameras are 23 rows so both lanes show entirely; the RSVP result spotlights only the genuine Accepted status for 2 s (1304–1366).

The restore is an atomic camera cut (camDur 0) together with the atomic state change on the closing-phrase attack. The camera never glides across the genuine recovery footer ('Message size unavailable: UnfinishedDraft', cleared only by Ctrl+S review). That footer stays outside the compose camera; no status retouch and no hidden post-restore key press.

RSVP dialog cameras are each state's exact native border box: review [9,4,78,13], accept [9,4,78,14], because the wrapped consequence adds one row. They are not identical cells, so rsvp.accept cuts the camera atomically (camDur 0) with its state. No fake border and no background fragments.

layout.headline: x 120, y 100, Adwaita Sans 800, 72 px
layout.subline: x 120, y 200, 34 px, typed on once per beat; ≤ 64 characters so it clears the key cue
layout.keyCue: right-aligned at x 1800, y 182, 20 frames before the real press; chords use '+', typed sequences sit side by side
layout.spotlight: warm wash on the bound ROI, padded 10 px horizontally and 3 px vertically
layout.cameraCut: a state with camDur 0 cuts the camera atomically with its state (rsvp.accept, draft.restored); all other state changes glide 18 frames
layout.nativeScale: k = min(box/ROI, 1 image px per CSS px, 34 px font ceiling)
layout.ember: x = frame left − 30 px, vertical travel only, rest beside the target row

narration.sub: From your contacts and recent mail. Only your pick is added.

qaContract.fields: qa(t).beat = {id, kind, phase (announce/read/demo/exit/intro/text/outro), announceStart, textSettled, demoStart, demoEnd, narration, keys}; qa(t).text; qa(t).textState = {opacity, settle}; qa(t).textMoving; qa(t).native = {visible, shots, assets, opacity}; qa(t).cameras[] = {shot, asset, roi, frame, scale, fontPx, opacity, moving, wrapper{scale, clip, opacity}, window, spot, target, exit}; qa(t).guide.margin; window.FILM_PLAN beats mirror this file
assertions: phase announce/read ⇒ no visible native frame
phase demo ⇒ narration equals the beat narration, band opacity 1 and settle 1 through demoEnd − 1
textMoving ⇒ no camera/wrapper motion on a visible frame outside exit
settled native text ≥ 26 px; spotlight target inside its camera window
ember glow never reaches native pixels (rest x + 33 px ≤ frame left + matte)
any roi-fallback on a visible asset is a failure

assetBinding.cameraRois: entry.cameraRois[name] for cameras; entry.rois[name] for spotlights
assetBinding.sessions: All states of one shot share one PTY grid and raster size; READY rejects a mixed shot
